scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Clouds are made of water, yet most of them just float. So what finally makes them rain?

scenes.name: rise
scenes.text: The sun heats the ground, and water evaporates. Warm, moist air rises, and cools as it goes higher.

scenes.name: condense
scenes.text: Cooler air can't hold as much water vapour, so it condenses into tiny droplets, around specks of dust, salt or smoke.

scenes.name: cloud
scenes.text: Billions of these droplets make a cloud. Each one is so tiny that rising air easily keeps it floating.

scenes.name: grow
scenes.text: Droplets bump into each other and merge. In cold clouds, ice crystals grow too, stealing water from the droplets around them.

scenes.name: fall
scenes.text: It takes around a million cloud droplets to build one raindrop. Once it's heavy enough, gravity wins, and it falls.

scenes.name: shape
scenes.text: Small raindrops are round, and bigger ones flatten into a bun shape as they fall. Not the teardrop we usually draw.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Rise, cool, condense, merge. That's rain. Follow for more on how things really work.
